draft.title: Positive and normative economics
card: A positive statement is about what is, was or will be. It can be tested against evidence, even if it turns out to be false.
A normative statement is about what should be. It rests on a value judgement, so evidence alone cannot settle it.
Words such as should, ought, fair and too much are signs of a normative statement.
Economists use positive analysis to show the likely effects of a policy. Deciding whether to adopt it is a normative choice.
draft.remember: Positive can be checked against evidence. Normative needs a value judgement.

a.q: Which of these statements is positive?
opts: Unemployment in Australia fell over the last year
Australia ought to spend more on public schools
Petrol taxes in Australia are far too high
It is unfair that rents rose so fast in Melbourne
a.why: Whether unemployment fell can be checked against the data. The other three use ought, too high and unfair, which are value judgements.
a.clue: Which one could you prove right or wrong with data?

b.q: Which of these statements is normative?
opts: Australia should raise its tobacco excise
A higher tobacco excise would cut smoking in Australia
Most Australians think tobacco excise is fair
Tobacco excise raises money for the Australian government
b.why: Should signals a value judgement. The prediction about smoking can be tested. A survey of what people think is positive too: it reports a fact about opinions, and it can be checked.
b.clue: A statement about what people believe can still be checked.

a.best: Unemployment in Australia fell over the last year

b.best: Australia should raise its tobacco excise

proposal.title: Positive and normative statements
card: A positive statement is about what is, was or will be. It can be tested against evidence, even if it turns out to be false.
A normative statement is about what should be. It rests on a value judgement, so evidence alone cannot settle it.
Words such as should, ought, fair and too much are signs of a normative statement. But a statement that reports what people believe, such as a survey result, is positive, because it can be checked.
Economists use positive analysis to show the likely effects of a policy. Deciding whether to adopt it is a normative choice.

b.q: Which of these statements is normative?
opts: Australia should raise its tobacco excise
A higher tobacco excise would cut smoking in Australia
Most Australians think tobacco excise is fair
Tobacco excise raises money for the Australian government
b.why: Should signals a value judgement about what ought to happen. The survey option uses the word fair, but it only reports what people believe, and a survey can check that, so it is positive. The other two are a testable prediction and a checkable fact.
